answer: Rhythm-gated admission. Each agent identity must sustain a low-variance heartbeat cadence for hours before earning any traffic weight; bursty arrivals stay quarantined in a harbor queue. The gate compares inter-arrival timing against a tundra-flat baseline, so faking N identities requires N parallel processes idling through the same slow warmup. Identity cost becomes wall-clock time plus concurrent connection overhead, scaling linearly and defeating cheap fan-out. A sonnet of steady packets, not volume, unlocks capacity.
